Ah, statistics. The easiest tool for liars.

Australia's homicide rate hasn't changed much since the gun ban, sexual assaults have been stagnant, and only robberies have seen a discernible decrease.

Source.

A few more stats on this page: http://www.nationaljournal.com/politics/15-things-to-know-about-australia-s-incredibly-effective-gun-clampdown-20121218 -- though it only goes up to 2006.

It's tricky to say. Figure "b" shows that both firearm and non-firearm homicides decreased dramatically since 1996, but they were already trending down beforehand. In the 1980s it appears that non-firearm homicides occured at roughly the same rate as firearm homicides, whereas now non-firearm homicides are about double firearm homicides. On the other hand, we're looking at very small numbers either way, and it's not clear how many of the murders "averted" by lack of a gun were really just converted into non-firearm murders. Anyway, we might be talking about saving a few lives a year. Which is nice, I guess, but insignificant compared to, say, airbags.

Suicide has also been trending downward nicely since the 1980s. Figure c shows the firearm suicide rate, which if you squint may or may not have a dip at 1996, but it's not actually as big as you'd think. The suicide rate is substantially larger than the murder rate in Australia, but the lack of a gun is probably even less likely to avert a suicide than it is to avert a murder.

So yeah. In the Australian context it's likely that taking a bunch of guns away at enormous expense has played some sort of role in decreasing the number of murders and suicides attributable to guns, but we're talking a handful of cases per year at most, and it's not clear how many of those are simply converted into non-firearm murders and suicides when firearms are unavailable. It's certainly true that murder and suicide are both way down since 1996, but that's bullshit use of statistics since that's part of a much broader trend (as seen in the equally massive decrease in non-firearm murders and suicides).
